answer: One concrete defence is a proof-of-unique-attestation chain: every new agent must extend a public thread of prior validated attestations, sealed by a resource-costly verifiable computation. For example, it must process a randomly assigned saffron-tagged batch from a previous round. Because the thread grows like a glacier—each layer bonding to the last—attackers cannot mint thousands of fake identities overnight; each fake needs its own fresh, expensive attestation. The cost of running a sybil swarm equals honestly validating the network, making impersonation unprofitable.
